questions.q: The interference pattern is obtained with two coherent light sources of intensity ratio $4: 1$. And the ratio $\dfrac{{I}_\max + {I}_\min}{{I}_\max - {I}_\min}$ is $\dfrac{5}{x}$. Then, the value of $x$ will be equal to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The ratio of the intensities is& $\dfrac{I1}{I2} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

After taking square root of above equation on both sides, we get,~$\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Apply componendo and dividendo,
$⇒ \dfrac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}} = \dfrac{2 + 1}{2 - 1} = \dfrac{3}{1}$
$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}\right)2 = \dfrac{Imax}{Imin} = \dfrac{9}{1} ⇒ \dfrac{{I}_\max + {I}_\min}{{I}_\max - {I}_\min} = \dfrac{10}{8} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

Therefore, the answer is~$4$.

questions.q: The ratio of intensities at two points $P$~and $Q$ on the screen in a Young's double slit experiment where phase difference between two waves of same amplitude are $\dfrac{π}{3}$ and $\dfrac{π}{2}$, respectively are
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

The formula to calculate the intensity of the interference pattern in Young's double slit experiment can be written as

$I = 4{I}_{0}\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{ϕ}{2}\right) . . .\left(1\right)$

Hence, the ratio of the required intensities can be calculated as follows-

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{I1}{I2}& = & \dfrac{4{I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)}{4{I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)}\\ & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{4}}{\dfrac{1}{2}}\\ & = & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Visible light of wavelength $6000 \times {10}^{- 8}cm$ falls normally on a single slit and produces a diffraction pattern. It is found that the second diffraction minimum is at ${60}^{o}$ from the central maximum. If the first minimum is produced at ${\theta}_{1},$ then ${\theta}_{1}$ is close to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For ${2}^{nd}$ minima,
$dsin ⁡ \theta = 2\lambda$
$sin ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{3}{2}$~,~(given)
$⇒ \dfrac{λ}{d} = \dfrac{3}{4}$~ ...(1)
So, for ${1}^{st}$ minima
$dsin\theta = \lambda$
$⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{λ}{d} = \dfrac{3}{4}$
$⇒ \theta = {25.65}^{o}$
$⇒ \theta \approx {25}^{o}$

questions.q: A system of three polarizers ${P}_{1}, {P}_{2}, {P}_{3}$ is set up such that the pass axis of ${P}_{3}$ is crossed with respect to that of ${P}_{1}$ . The pass axis of ${P}_{2}$ is inclined at ${60}^{o}$ to the pass axis of ${P}_{3} .$ When a beam of unpolarized light of intensity ${I}_{o}$ is incident on ${P}_{1},$ the intensity of light transmitted by the three polarizers is $I$ . The ratio  \left({I}_{o} / I\right)$ equals (nearly):$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The intensity of light coming out of 1st Polaroid will be ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}$
From Malus law $I = {I}_{0}\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta$
From Polaroid 2: $I = \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}\cos^{2} ⁡ 30 ° = \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{8}$
From Polaroid 3: $I = \dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{8}\cos^{2} ⁡ 60 ° = \dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{8}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{32}$
Now, $\dfrac{{I}_{0}}{I} = \dfrac{32}{3} = 10.67$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, the source is white light. One of the slits is covered by red filter and another by a green filter. In this case
options: There shall be an interference pattern for red distinct from that for green.
There shall be no interference fringes.
There shall be alternate interference fringes of red and green.
There shall be an interference pattern, where each fringe's pattern center is green and outer edges is red.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Different colours will have different fringe width. Within a few fringes of red, there will be several fringes of violet.
Also, there will be overlapping of colours.

questions.q: When a polaroid sheet is rotated between two crossed polaroids then the transmitted light intensity will be maximum for a rotation of :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Let ${I}_{0}$ be intensity of unpolarised light incident on first polaroid.
${I}_{1} =$ Intensity of light transmitted from ${1}^{st}$ polaroid
$= \dfrac{I0}{2}$
If $\theta$ be the angle between ${1}^{st}$ and ${2}^{nd}$ polaroid and $ϕ$ be the angle between ${2}^{nd}$ and ${3}^{rd}$ polaroid, then

$\theta + ϕ = 90 ° . . . \left(1\right)$

If ${I}_{2} =$ Intensity from ${2}^{nd}$ polaroid,

\begin{cases}{I}_{2}$& = & {I}_{1}cos^{2}\theta\\ & = & $\d$dfrac{I0}{2}cos^{2}\theta\end{cases}

If ${I}_{3} =$ Intensity from ${3}^{rd}$ polaroid

$\begin{cases}{I}_{3} & = & {I}_{2}cos^{2}ϕ \\ & = & ${I}_{1}\cos^{2}\theta\cos^{2}$ϕ \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{I0}{2}cos^{2}\$thetacos^{2} \left($90 ° - $\theta\right)$\\ & = & \dfrac{I0}{2}cos^{2}\thetasin^{2}\theta\\ & = & \dfrac{I0}{2} \left[\dfrac{2sin\thetacos\theta}{2}\right]$2 \\ & = & $\dfrac{I0}{8}\sin^{2}$2$\theta\end{cases}

Now, ${I}_{3}$ will be maximum when

$sin2$\theta =$1$

$⇒ 2$\theta =$90 °$

$⇒ $\theta =$45 °$

$

questions.q: Two coherent sources of light interfere. The intensity ratio of two sources is $1: 4$. For this interference pattern if the value of $\dfrac{{I}_\max + {I}_\min}{{I}_\max - {I}_\min}$ is equal to $\dfrac{2\alpha + 1}{\beta + 3}$, then $\dfrac{α}{β}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $\dfrac{I1}{I2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$~or~${I}_{2} = 4{I}_{1}$

Maximum intensity is~${I}_\max = \left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)2 = {I}_{1} + 4{I}_{1} + 2\sqrt{{I}_{1}4{I}_{1}} = 9{I}_{1}$

Minimum intensity is~${I}_\min = \left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)2 = {I}_{1} + 4{I}_{1} - 2\sqrt{{I}_{1}4{I}_{1}} = {I}_{1}$

The ratio of~$\dfrac{{I}_\max + {I}_\min}{{I}_\max - {I}_\min}$~is~

~$\dfrac{9{I}_{1} + {I}_{1}}{9{I}_{1} - {I}_{1}} = \dfrac{10}{8} = \dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{2\alpha + 1}{\beta + 3}$

$\alpha = 2\beta = 1$

$∴ \dfrac{α}{β} = \dfrac{2}{1} = 2$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : The beam of electrons shows wave nature and exhibit interference and diffraction.

Reason R : Davisson Germer Experimentally verified the wave nature of electrons.

In the light of the above statements. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct but R is Not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The Davisson-Germer experiment showed that electron beams can undergo diffraction when passed through the atomic crystals. This shows that the wave nature of electrons. When electron is& in wave nature& it can exhibit interference and show diffraction.

Hence,& Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

The difference between the largest fringe width and the smallest fringe width obtained over time is given as:
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: When unpolarized light is incident at an angle of $60 °$ on a transparent medium from air. The reflected ray is completely polarized. The angle of refraction in the medium is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By Brewster’s law at complete polarization, refracted ray and reflected ray are perpendicular to each other.

As angle of reflection will be $= 60 °$. Therefore, angle of refraction will be $= 180 ° - 60 ° - 90 ° = 30 °$.

questions.q: Two light waves having the same wavelength $\lambda$ in vacuum are in phase initially. Then the first wave travels a path ${L}_{1}$ through a medium of refractive index ${n}_{1}$while the second wave travels a path of length~${L}_{2}$ through a medium of refractive index ${n}_{2}$. After this the phase difference between the two waves is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The optical path between any two points is proportional to the time of travel.

The distance traversed by light in a medium of refractive index& $\mu$~in time~$t$~is given by~$d = vt$~.......(i)

Where~$v$~is velocity of light in the medium. The distance traversed by light in a vacuum in this time,

$s = ct$

$= c \times \dfrac{d}{v}$~ ~[from equation (i)]

$= d\dfrac{c}{v} = \mu d$~.....(ii) (Since$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v}$)

This distance is the equivalent distance in vacuum and is called optical path.

Here, optical path for first ray~$= {n}_{1}{L}_{1}$

Optical path for second ray~$= {n}_{2}{L}_{2}$

Path difference~$= {n}_{1}{L}_{1} - {n}_{2}{L}_{2}$

Now, phase difference~$= \dfrac{2\pi}{λ} \times$path difference

$= \dfrac{2\pi}{λ} \times \left({n}_{1}{L}_{1} - {n}_{2}{L}_{2}\right)

$

questions.q: Which of the following phenomena can not be explained by wave theory of light?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Compton effect refers to scattering of a photon by free electrons. This phenomenon provides an evidence for particle nature of light.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, if the source of light changes from orange to blue then:
options: the central bright fringe will become a dark fringe.
the distance between consecutive fringes will decrease.
the distance between consecutive fringes will increase.
the intensity of the minima will increase.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fringe width $= \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$.
As $\lambda$ decreases, fringe width also decreases.

questions.q: Consider a tank made of glass (refractive index $1.5$ ) with a thick bottom. It is filled with a liquid of refractive index $\mu .$ A student finds that, irrespective of what the incident angle $i$ (see figure) is for a beam of light entering the liquid, the light reflected from the liquid glass interface is never completely polarized. For this to happen, the minimum value of $\mu$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For reflected light not be completely polarized,

$tan ⁡ r \ne \dfrac{{\mu}_{g}}{{\mu}_{w}} = \dfrac{1.5}{\mu}$

For minimum $\mur$ is maximum. $r$ is maximum when $i$ is maximum i.e. $i = {90}^{o}$

$⇒ sin ⁡ r = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$

$⇒ tan ⁡ r = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{\mu}^{2} - 1}}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{\mu}^{2} - 1}} = \dfrac{1.5}{\mu}$

$⇒ {\mu}^{2} = 2.25 \left({\mu}^{2} -1\right)$

$⇒ 1.25{\mu}^{2} = 2.25$

$⇒ \mu = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2.25}{1.25}}

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{5}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{5}}$

questions.q: Two coherent sources of sound, ${S}_{1}$ and ${S}_{2},$ produce sound waves of the same wavelength $\lambda = 1m$~are~in phase. ${S}_{1}$~and ${S}_{2}$~are placed $1 . 5m$ apart (see fig). A listener, located at $L$, directly in front of ${S}_{2}$, finds that the intensity is at a minimum when he is $2m$ away from ${S}_{2}$. The listener moves away from ${S}_{1}$, keeping the distance from ${S}_{2}$ fixed. The adjacent maximum of intensity is observed when the listener is at a distance~$d$ from ${S}_{1}$. Then~$d$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Two sources od same wavelength,& $\lambda = 1m$

Distance between two sources,${S}_{1}{S}_{2} = 1 . 5m$

Distance of listener from the source~${S}_{2}$,~${S}_{2}L = 2m$

Condition for minimum intensity, at~$2m$~is

Path difference,~$P . D . = ( 2n + 1 ) \dfrac{λ}{2} . . . ( 1 )$

$⇒ P . D . = \sqrt{{2}^{2} + ( 1 . 5{)}^{2}} = ( 2n + 1 ) \dfrac{λ}{2}$
$⇒ 2 . 5 = ( 2n + 1 ) \dfrac{λ}{2} . . . ( 1 )$

Now, the path difference between the rays is so that the adjacent~maxima is obtained,

$P . D . = d - 2 = n\lambda . . . ( 2 )$

The path difference between adjacent maxima and minima is~$\dfrac{λ}{2}$, form equation (1) and (2) we get,

$( d - 2 ) - 2 . 5 = \dfrac{λ}{2} . . . ( 3 )$
$⇒ d - 2 = 2 . 5 + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ d = 5m$

questions.q: A wave of frequency& $= 3GHz$,~strikes a particle of size~\left(\dfrac{1}{100}\right)th$~of~$\lambda$, \text{ and } then this phenomenon is called as$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Rayleigh scattering applies to particles that are small with respect to wavelengths of light.

questions.q: The figure shows a Young's double slit experimental setup. It is observed that when a thin transparent sheet of thickness t and refractive index $\mu$ is put in front of one of the slits, the central maximum gets shifted by a distance equal to n fringe width. If the wavelength of light used is $\lambda$~then $t$& will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Shift in central maxima $= \dfrac{D}{a}\left(\mu - 1\right)t$
Fringe width $= \dfrac{D\lambda}{a}$
It's given,
$\dfrac{D}{a}\left(\mu - 1\right)t = n\dfrac{D\lambda}{a}$
$t = \dfrac{n\lambda}{\mu - 1}$

questions.q: A beam of plane polarized light of large cross-sectional area and uniform intensity of $3 .3 Wm^{– 2}$ falls normally on a polarizer (cross-sectional area $3 \times {10}^{– 4}m^{2}$), which rotates about its axis with an angular speed of $31 .4 rads^{- 1}$. The energy of light passing through the polarizer per revolution, is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Intensity of plane polarized light& of large cross-sectional area is& ${I}_{0} = 3 . 3Wm^{- 2}$

Area of cross-section of polarizer is~$A = 3 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}$

Angular speed of rotation is~$\omega = 31 . 4rads^{- 1}$

The intensity of light is the given by the definition,

~$I = \dfrac{E}{AT} . . . ( 1 )$

Intensity of light passing through the polarizer as polarizer rotates is given by

${I}_{avg} = {I}_{0}\dfrac{1}{T}{∫}_{0}^{T}\cos^{2}\left(\omegat\right) d t$

$⇒ {I}_{avg} = {I}_{0}\dfrac{1}{T}{∫}_{0}^{T}\left[\dfrac{1 + cos\left(2\omegat\right)}{2}\right] d t$

$⇒ {I}_{avg} = {I}_{0}\dfrac{1}{2T} \left[{∫}_{0}^{T}d t + {∫}_{0}^{T}cos\left(2\omegat\right) d t\right]$

$⇒ {I}_{avg} = ${I}_{0}\dfrac{1}{2T} \left[T + 0\right]$

$⇒ {I}_{avg} = $\dfrac{I0}{2} . . . ($2 )$

Using equation (1) and (2) we get energy per revolution is given by

$E = $\dfrac{{I}_{0}A}{2}$T = $\dfrac{{I}_{0}A}{2}\dfrac{2\pi}{ω}

$E = $\dfrac{3 .3 \times 3 \times {10}^{- 4}}{2}\dfrac{3 . 14}{31 . 4}

$E ≃ 1 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

$

questions.q: Two coherent sources produce waves of different intensities which interfere. After interference, the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity is $16 .$ The intensity of the waves are in the ratio:
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: The diffraction pattern of a light of wavelength $400$ nm diffracting from a slit of width $0 . 2mm$ is focused on the focal plane of a convex lens of focal length $100$ cm. The width of the ${1}^{st}$ secondary maxima will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Width of ${1}^{st}$ secondary maxima $= \dfrac{λ}{a} \cdot D$

Here

$a = 0 . 2 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

$\lambda = 400 \times {10}^{- 9}m$

$D = 100 \times {10}^{- 2} = 1m$

Therefore, width of ${1}^{st}$ secondary maxima

$= \dfrac{400 \times {10}^{- 9}}{0 . 2 \times {10}^{- 3}} \times 1$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 3}m = 2mm$

questions.q: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities I and $4 \mathrm{I}$ are superimposed. The difference between maximum and minimum possible intensities in the resulting beam is $x \mathrm{I}$. The value of $x$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I_{\max }=(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}}+\sqrt{4 \mathrm{I}})^2=9 \mathrm{I} \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\min }=(\sqrt{4 \mathrm{I}}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}})^2=\mathrm{I} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}_{\max }-\mathrm{I}_{\min }=8 \mathrm{I}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a double slit experiment with monochromatic light, fringes are obtained on a screen placed at some distance from the plane of slits. If the screen is moved by $5 \times {10}^{- 2}m$ towards the slits, the change in fringe width is $3 \times {10}^{- 3}cm$. If the distance between the slits is $1$ mm, then the wavelength of the light will be____nm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that the fringe width in YDSE is& $\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$

$⇒ \Delta\beta = \dfrac{λ}{d}\Delta D$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{\left(\Delta\beta\right)d}{\Delta D} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{- 3} \times {10}^{- 2} \times {10}^{- 3}}{5 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 6 \times {10}^{- 7}m = 600nm$

questions.q: Orange light of wavelength $6000 \times {10}^{– 10}m$~illuminates a single slit of width~$0 . 6 \times {10}^{– 4}m$.& The maximum possible number of diffraction minima produced on both sides of the central maximum is __________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Light of wavelength& $6000 \times {10}^{– 10}m$ passes through a single slit of width $0 . 6 \times {10}^{– 4}m$. Find height of highest order of minima on both side central maxima

for minima~

$dsin \theta = n \lambda$

$sin \theta = \dfrac{nλ}{d} < 1$

$n \le \dfrac{d}{λ}$

$n < \dfrac{0 . 6 \times {10}^{- 4}}{6000 \times {10}^{- 10}}$

$n < 100$

The total number of maxima of both side at central maxima~$= 100 + 100 = 200$&

questions.q: Unpolarised light of intensity $32Wm^{- 2}$~passes through the combination of three polaroids such that the pass axis of the last polaroids is perpendicular to that of the pass axis of first polaroids. If intensity of emerging light is $3Wm^{- 2}$, then the angle between pass axis of first two polaroids is _________°.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is

& ${I}_{0} = 32Wm^{- 2}$

${I}_{f} = 3Wm^{- 2}$

Thus, by substituting the value, we get

${I}_{f} = \left(\dfrac{I0}{2}\cos^{2}\theta\right) \times \cos^{2} \left($90 ° - $\theta\right) . . . ($i )$

$⇒ 3 = 16\left(\cos^{2}\theta \cdot \sin^{2}\theta\right)

$⇒ cos$\theta \cdot$sin$\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$⇒ sin2$\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}$⇒ $\theta =$30 °$

questions.q: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities 4I and 9I are superimposed. The difference between the maximum and minimum intensities in the resulting interference pattern is xI. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_{\max }=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2}\right)^2 \\ & =(\sqrt{4 \mathrm{I}}+\sqrt{9 \mathrm{I}})^2=25 \mathrm{I} \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\min }=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2}\right)^2 \\ & =(\sqrt{4 \mathrm{I}}-\sqrt{9 \mathrm{I}})^2=\mathrm{I} \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\max }-\mathrm{I}_{\min }=24 \mathrm{I} \\ & \mathrm{x}=24\end{aligned}$
